title: Assassin's Creed Nexus VR
owned: Owner of multiple missions, with support from other level designers: Mission 2, Return to Monteriggioni; Mission 3, Monteriggioni Tunnels; Mission 4, To Save the City; and Mission 13, Return of the Cult of Hermes. Two of them end to end.
brief: Design Assassin's Creed missions for VR, where the player has hands and a head instead of a controller and scale, sightlines and readability all behave differently.
problem: The layout of the city could not be changed, so the missions had to be built inside it with dense, legible spaces that support more than one route: stealth as the intended path, combat as the fallback.
approach: Mission design, flow and level-design ingredients across four missions.
result: Shipped VR missions, two of them owned end to end.
reflection: VR punishes anything you can't read at a glance — designing for a body, not a camera, sharpened how I think about sightlines everywhere since.
summary: Designed mission levels and encounter spaces across four missions, including two end-to-end.

gallery.caption: Cult of Hermes dock market, mission 13. I pitched a three-finger dock structure: three readable macro approaches with smaller connections, hiding spaces and traversal options. Mission design and implementation within a collaborative Ubisoft production.

gallery.caption: Venice clocktower puzzle space. I designed a compact puzzle space around reachable mechanisms, back-and-forth movement and the historical identity of the tower.

gallery.caption: Combat and mission sequence, Monteriggioni Tunnels. I implemented a wave-based combat sequence that culminated in a larger knight encounter, with mission logic connected to animation, VFX and audio hooks.
